doc.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta and Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1958-08-26

title: Searching for Wade Whaley
summary: Ory last saw Wade Whaley in 1945 in Watts; the interviewer asks if he might be in San Diego or San Jose.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: There was a Columbia recording. Uh-huh. Well, I asked you the other night on the phone about Wade Whaley. You think he's in San Diego. Do you? Where did you see him last?
Last time I saw him there, in 45, I was working at the Jade Room. My client had to go to Seattle, Joe, Dennisburg, you know?
And he had some business center, so I'd wait for a few nights, you know?

And he was living in a project there in Watts. And I went there and I said, we used to go to work. He was working days, you know? And uh, his wife said, if you do work, you have to keep it quiet because you have a job in the shipyard or something. I said, what difference does that make? I said, uh, you can do ten jobs as long as you do his work on the other job, you know? Yeah. So he's got to be a henpeck, you know? Yeah. And uh, he played until Joe came back and I haven't seen him since. No.
We haven't been able to hear anything about him. Nobody knows where he is. No.
Your girl's calling. She's out there. Girl's calling. She's on there. Have you ever heard that he was around San Jose? Who? Wait, wait, wait, wait.
He wasn't San Jose before he moved down there. Before then. Because his banjo, the secretary of the union here used to play banjo with him. He died about two years ago. Forbes. Yeah, Forbes.
He said he didn't know where he was located. I don't know if he's dead or what.
Gee, is it two years since Forbes died? Huh? It doesn't seem like two years since Forbes died. No, I didn't say two years.
Well, you talked to him two years ago about it. About it, yeah.
Yeah. I was in Los Angeles when he thought about it. That's just by a little over a year.
Yeah, I was thinking about a year.
I was at Beverly Cavern then when he died. He died during the strike. The cemetery strike? Yeah.
